#Features/_style tag designates the item as a _style item_ such that its `css_style` block is automatically installed/updated on the page (under `<head><style …>`). In addition, any [dependents](#dependencies) of the style item are automatically styled (on their `<div class="item …">`) using a special CSS class name derived from the style item name as in `dep_<name>`. Any invalid characters (outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`) are replaced with `_`.

#MindPage/core/functions are:
- #load function for loading external libraries.
- #macros attached to `window`, e.g. `html(content)`.
- #MindBox functions, e.g. `set(text)`.
- `_item(name,[log_errors])` returns [_Item](#MindPage/core/_item) with name (label or id).
- `_items([label])` returns array of [_Items](#MindPage/core/_item).
- `_exists(name,[allow_multiple])` returns true if item `name` exists.
- `_create(text,[options])` creates new item w/ given text.
- `_labels([selector])` returns array of labels matching optional selector.
- `_sublabels(parent)` returns array of labels nested under parent label.
- `_host` returns (canonical) hostname for client
- `_is_local(host)` returns true if `host` is considered local
- [_modal](#MindPage/core/functions/_modal) opens modal confirmation/input prompts.
- `_delay(ms)` returns promise resolved after specified time.
- `_update_dom()` returns promise resolved after dom is up-to-date.
- `_scroll_to(y)` scroll vertically to position `y`.
- `_encrypt(text)` encrypts a (text) string.
- `_decrypt(text)` decrypts an encrypted (text) string.
- `_encrypt_bytes(uint8array)` encrypts an byte array.
- `_decrypt_bytes(uint8array)` decrypts an encrypted byte array.
- `_encrypt_item(item)` encrypts an item.
- `_decrypt_item(item)` decrypts an encrypted item.
- `_render_item(item)` renders an item.
- `_parse_tags(text)` parses tags in `text`.
- `_parse_label(text)` parses label in `text`.
- `_replace_tags(text, regex, replacer)` replaces tags in `text`.
- `_resolve_tags(label, tags)` resolves `tags` relative to `label`.
- `_resolve_tag(label, tag)` resolves `tag` relative to `label`.
- `_special_tag(tag)` returns if `tag` enables any #features.
- `_extract_block(text, type)` extracts block(s) in `text`.
- `_replace_block(text, type, replacer)` replaces block(s) in `text`.
- `_stringify(x)` converts `x` to a string.
- `_byte_stringify(x)` converts `x` to a byte (binary) string.
- `_encode(string,[encoding='base64'])` encodes `string` into `encoding`:
  - `'base64'` string, `'utf8'` string, `'utf8_array'` (`Uint8Array`), or `'byte_array'` (`Uint8Array`).
- `_decode(encoded,[encoding='base64'])` decodes string from specified encoding.
- `_concat_byte_arrays(...arrays)` concatenates byte arrays.
- `_hash(x,[hasher],[stringifier])` hashes `x` using `hasher` and `stringifier`. Default hasher is `_hash_64_fnv1a` (see below) and default stringifier is `toString` for functions and `JSON.stringify` for everything else. Returns integer (≤52-bit) or hex string (>52-bit) depending on `hasher`:
  - `_hash_32_djb2(string)` hashes using [djb2](http://www.cse.yorku.ca/~oz/hash.html) (xor variant).
  - `_hash_32_fnv1a(string)` hashes using 32-bit [fnv-1a](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fowler–Noll–Vo_hash_function).
  - `_hash_32_murmur3(string)` hashes using 32-bit [murmur v3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MurmurHash).
  - `_hash_52_fnv1a(string)` hashes using 52-bit [fnv-1a](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fowler–Noll–Vo_hash_function).
  - `_hash_64_fnv1a(string)` hashes using 64-bit [fnv-1a](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fowler–Noll–Vo_hash_function).
  - `_hash_128_murmur3_x64(string)` hashes using 128-bit [murmur v3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MurmurHash) (x64 variant).
  - `_hash_128_murmur3_x86(string)` hashes using 128-bit [murmur v3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MurmurHash) (x86 variant).
  - `_hash_160_sha1(string)` hashes using 160-bit [secure hash algo 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1).

#animations/brownian_motion
- Velocity of molecular motion
- SDE: $`dX_t = \mu_t dt + \sigma dW_t`$
```js
const sigma = 0.05 // inverse mass of particle
const tail = 10    // past length in seconds
const drift = (t) => ({ // ∞-shaped periodic drift
  x: Math.cos(.5 * t * 2*Math.PI),
  y: 1.5 * Math.cos(t * 2*Math.PI)
})
```
<<animation(draw, {period:0, reset:true, init})>>
```js_removed
let t0 = 0
let x = .5, y = .5 // start in center
let path = [[x,y]]
const maxPoints = tail * 60
function draw(ctx, t, w, h) {
  if (t > t0 + .1) { t0 = t; return } // ignore big time steps
  if (t < t0) { t0 = 0; x = .5; y = .5; path = [[x,y]] } // reset
  // update position, time, tail
  const W = jStat.normal(0,sigma*Math.sqrt(t-t0))
  const mu = drift(t)
  x += W.sample() + mu.x * (t-t0)
  y += W.sample() + mu.y * (t-t0)
  t0 = t
  path.push([x,y])
  while (path.length > maxPoints) path.shift()
  // draw tail
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h)
  ctx.strokeStyle = 'white'
  ctx.lineWidth = 3
  for (let i=0; i<path.length-1; ++i) {
    ctx.globalAlpha = (i+1)/path.length
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.moveTo(path[i][0]*w, path[i][1]*h)
    ctx.lineTo(path[i+1][0]*w,path[i+1][1]*h)
    ctx.stroke()
  }
  // draw particle
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1  
  ctx.fillStyle = 'white'
  ctx.beginPath()
  ctx.arc(w*x, h*y, 10, 0, 2*Math.PI)
  ctx.fill()
}
// initializer to ensure jStat is loaded
async function init(canvas) {
  await _load(window.jStat || "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jstat@latest/dist/jstat.min.js")
  return canvas.getContext('2d')
}
```

#features/_listen tag enables code to be evaluated on certain events:
- `_on_change(text)` is evaluated at each change to #MindBox triggered by user typing in, or programmatically. Text can be empty.
- `_on_search(text)` is evaluated at each new search via #MindBox triggered by user typing in (subject to debounce), or programmatically. Search text can be empty.
- `_on_create(text)` is evaluated each time new text is submitted on #MindBox using `create` button, keyboard shortcut, or programmatically.
- ``_on_command_<name>(`…`)`` is evaluated when [command](#commands) `/name …` is submitted on #MindBox. Argument `…` can be empty. Valid return values are in listed in #commands.
- `_on_focus()` is evaluated each time MindPage window (or tab) is "focused" to receive keyboard, touch, or other input.
- `_on_item_change(id, label, prev_label, deleted, remote, dependency)` is evaluated at each change to an item or its dependencies.
- `_on_local_store_change(id)` is evaluated at each change to `local_store` of an item.
- `_on_global_store_change(id, remote)` is evaluated at each change to `global_store` of an item.
- `_on_attr_change(id, remote)` is evaluated at each change to `attr` of an item.
- Example code:
```js_example
function _on_search(text) { alert("You searched for: " + text) }
function _on_create(text) { alert("You created: " + text) }
```

#features/_async tag enables _async_ evaluation.
- Code is wrapped as `_this.start(async()=>{ ... })`
- Code must explicitly `return` any output.
- Code must `await` on promises to avoid premature return.
- Default log attribution is time-based (vs stack-based).
  - Allows easy tracking of logs from external libraries.
  - Upon return, logs are written into item via `write_log`.
  - Log options can be configured via `_this.log_options`.
- Item may not be on the stack for entire async evaluation.
  - Item is always on stack for top-level async function call.
  - Helper functions can bring item back on stack as needed.
    - `invoke`, `attach`, `dispatch`, `promise`, `resolve`, ...
    - For logging: `debug`, `info`, `log`, `warn`, `error`
  - `_this` is still available from _lexical context_ of item.
- Async evaluation is _propagated to [dependents](#dependencies)_.
  - For example, see #mathjs/example.
#Features/_autorun tag enables item to be auto-run on changes to #dependencies.

#macros are #code that generate content. - Syntax is `\<<...>>` where `...` is #code. - Output is treated same as typed-in content. - HTML content can be wrapped in `_html` block - See convenient `html(…)` macro below. - #features/_init can be used for _global_ macros. - #dependencies become optional, for auto-updating. - Examples: - `\<>` from #code #_code gives: <> - #/bar_chart macro in #charts. - #/graph macro in #graphs. - #/animation macro in #animations. - Basic macros (import as `#_macros`): ```js const px = (s) => typeof s == 'number' ? s+'px' : s const img = (u, w='auto', h='auto', style='') => `` const code = (text) => "`" + text + "`" const block = (type, content) => '```'+type+'\n' + content + '\n```' const html = (content) => block('_html', content) const json = (obj) => block('json',JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2) ?.replace(/"([^"]+)":/g,'$1:')/*?.replace(/,([^\s\d])/g,", $1")*/) // NOTE: using onmousedown + cancelled onclick maintains keyboard focus and is generally more robust, especially on mobile devices w/ virtual keyboards const jslink = (js, text=js, classes='', style='', title=js) => `${text}` const evallink = (item, js, text=js, classes='', style='', title=js) => jslink(`_item('${item.id}')` + '.eval(`' + js.replace(/([`\\$])/g,"\\$1") + '`)', text, classes, style, title) const cmdlink = (cmd, text=cmd, options='', classes='', style='', title=cmd) => jslink(`MindBox.create(\`${cmd}\`,{${options}})`, text, classes, style, title) const spacer = (height=10, width=10) => `
` const time_short = (ms) => ( ms < 60*1000 ? "<1m" : ms < 60*60*1000 ? Math.floor(ms/(60*1000)) + "m" : ms < 24*60*60*1000 ? Math.floor(ms/(60*60*1000)) + "h" : Math.floor(ms/(24*60*60*1000)) + "d" ) // register most common macros globally // importing via #_macros is optional for auto-updating // also allows _this to refer to invoking item (vs #macros) as expected // we avoid use of _this in global macros to avoid this ambiguity function _init() { window.img = img window.code = code window.block = block window.html = html window.json = json window.jslink = jslink window.evallink = evallink window.cmdlink = cmdlink window.spacer = spacer } ``` #_init

#MindPage/core/_Item object holds a reference to a MindPage item and provides access to a wide range of [properties](#MindPage/core/properties) and functions:
- `eval([js, options])` evaluates code in context of item.
- `eval_macros(text, [options])` evaluates macros in given text.
- `read([type, options])` reads text from item.
- `read_deep(type, [options])` reads text from item + dependencies.
- `read_input(type, [options])` reads input from item + dependencies.
- `write(text, [type], [options])` writes text into item.
- `clear(type)` clears blocks in item.
- `remove(type)` removes blocks in item.
- `delete([confirm])` deletes item.
- `get_log([options])` returns console log messages for item.
- `write_log([options])` writes log messages into item.
- `show_logs(autohide_after)` shows and auto-hides log messages.
- `hide_logs()` hides log messages.
- `show_status([status], [progress])` shows status on running item.
- `clear_status()` clears (and hides) status on item
- `touch([save=false])` updates (and optionally saves) time of item.
- `save()` saves item.
- `start(async_func)` starts async evaluation on item.
- `invoke(func)` invokes function with item on the stack.
- `attach(func)` attaches function to item by wrapping it with `invoke`.
- `attach(promise)` attaches promise to item by wrapping `then`,`catch`,`finally`.
- `dispatch(func, [delay_ms])` dispatches _attached_ function.
- `dispatch_task(name, func, [delay_ms, period_ms])` dispatches named task.
- `cancel_task(name)` cancels named task.
- `pending_task(name)` returns true if named task is pending completion.
- `promise(func)` returns new attached promise with attached executor.
- `resolve(thing)` returns new attached promise that resolves `thing`.
- `debug|info|log|warn|error(...)` invokes attached `console.*(...)`.
- `fatal(...)` throws `Error(...)` including stack trace.
- `delay(ms)` returns promise resolved after specified time.
- `images([options])` returns array of uploaded images.
- `invalidate_elem_cache()` invalidates rendered element cache for item.
- `cached(key, value_function)` returns cached value from `item.cache`.
- `invalidate_cache()` invalidates cache for next access via `item.cache`.
- `validate_cache()` validates cache for current `item.deephash`.
- `save_local_store()` saves `item.local_store` to `localStorage`.
- `save_global_store()` saves `item.global_store` to `firebase`.

#commands are #code run via #MindBox. Examples: #/hello #/hello_again #/js #/alert #/copy #/export #/restore #/agenda #/invert #/weight.
- Type command as `/name …` and hit #⇧⏎.
- Evaluates ``run(`…`)`` from item named `#commands/<name>`.
  - If missing, evaluates ``_on_command_<name>(`…`)`` in [listeners](#features/_listen).
  - Function can be `async` or return promise, e.g. #/agenda.
- Return nothing (or `undefined`) to clear text and defocus.
- Return string (can be empty) to replace text.
- Return object `{ text:"…" }` to create new item.
  - `edit:true|false` to start editing created item.
  - `run:true|false` to run `js_input` in item.
  - `init:(item)=>{...}` to initialize item.
- Return `null` or [_Item](#MindPage/core/_Item) to do nothing.
  - Allows command to handle any changes to #MindBox as needed.
- Commands can also be triggered programmatically.
  - e.g. via [window._create](#MindPage/core/functions) or [MindBox.create](#MindBox).
  - Any created or returned [_Item](#MindPage/core/_Item) (or `null`) is also returned to the programmatic context where command is triggered.

#commands/copy command `/copy name` copies an item. Item `name` can be specified as either `#label` or `id`. For example, this item can be specified as either `<<_this.label>>` or `<<_this.id>>`.
```js
const run = (name) => ({text:_item(name).read()})
```

#features/_welcome tag enables "welcome" code to be evaluated _after_ the initial page has been rendered and any welcome [modal](#MindPage/core/functions/_modal) has been dismissed.

#private means that your items are readable **only by you, on your devices**. This is achieved using encryption based on a _personal secret_ that is never sent or stored anywhere, as can be verified from [open source code](https://github.com/olcan/mind.page). This is much more private than using authentication alone, which still leaves your content readable to service providers, who often also use closed source code that can not be verified.

#items/ordering is determined primarily by _recency_ as you edit or interact with items, and _relevance_ as you type into #MindBox.
- Navigate using [tags](#items/tagging) or keywords to bring items up.
  - Use `back` button to restore a previous ordering.
- Edit/save item to move it up permanently.
  - Alternatively tap item number (upper right).
- [Log items](#features/log) preserve their position in time.

#MindPage/core/functions/_modal opens a modal window for basic confirmation and input prompts. Programmable click handlers can be used to trigger certain actions that can otherwise be disallowed in some browsers (e.g. iOS Safari), such as:
- `window.open` for API authorization (OAuth) flows, e.g. #gapi.
- `HTMLElement.focus` to focus on input elements, e.g. #/example:
Can be closed or updated using global functions `_modal_close([modal],[output])` and `_modal_update(modal, options)`. Visibility can be checked using `_modal_visible([modal])`.
Can also be used to work around a [known issue](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38083702/alert-confirm-and-prompt-not-working-after-using-history-api-on-safari-ios) with `alert`/`confirm`/`prompt` dialogs not working after using browser history (e.g. going back/forward) in iOS. `_modal_alert(msg, [done])`, `_modal_confirm(msg, [confirmed], [cancelled])`, and `_modal_prompt(msg, [default], [confirmed], [cancelled])` can be used as convenient async replacements.

#features/_init tag enables initialization code.
- `_init()` function is evaluated _once_ during page load.
  - Read from `js_init` block if it exists (otherwise from `js`).
  - Ignores #dependencies (assumed self-contained).
- Ideal for extending external libraries (e.g. #c3, #graphviz).
- Ideal for triggering #load for dynamically loaded libraries. 
- New or modified `_init` functions require reload to take effect.
- Example initialization code:
```js_example
function _init() { console.log("Welcome to MindPage!") }
```

#features/_debug tag disables all code wrapping (e.g. for #features/_async) to enable debugging commands such as #commands/debug.

#features/_context tag enables item to be brought up as `context` for other items that are tagged in it. This feature is similar to using [nested](#items/naming/nested) names but allows arbitrary names as long as they are unique.
#features/_menu tag enables special styling where tags and links expand to make them as large as possible for easy tapping.

#features/_pin tag _pins_ item at the top.
- Pinned items can also be [dotted](#/dot).
- An optional suffix `#_pin/...` can be used for [natural ordering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_sort_order).
- An optional prefix `#_context/pin/...` can be used to specify _context_.
  - Item is pinned only when this context is being navigated.

- Hide tags using underscore prefix, e.g. `#_tag`.
